title: FRP Grating Load Table & Span Calculator: Engineering Data for 25/30/38/50mm
author: Structural Engineering
excerpt: Complete load/span tables for FRP molded grating (25mm, 30mm, 38mm, 50mm) and pultruded grating — uniform load, point load, deflection limits, safety factors, and engineering calculation methodology.
content:
1. Engineering Principles & Design Standards

FRP grating design follows ASTM D3916 (pultruded shapes), EUROCOMP design code, and FGMC (Fiberglass Grating Manufacturers Council) guidelines. Key design considerations: allowable stress design (ASD) with safety factors, deflection limits (typically L/200 for floors, L/240 for sensitive areas), creep analysis for long-term loads, thermal effects, and connection design. Unlike steel, FRP is orthotropic (different properties in different directions), so bidirectional molded grating has equal strength in both directions, while pultruded grating is strongest in the bearing bar direction. Safety factors: 2.5-3.0 for ultimate strength, 1.5 for serviceability (deflection).

2. Molded Grating Load Table (38mm, 38×38mm mesh, Isophthalic)

Span 600mm: Uniform load 5.0 kN/m², Point load 1.5 kN, Deflection <3mm, Safety factor 3.0. Span 800mm: Uniform load 4.0 kN/m², Point load 1.2 kN, Deflection <4mm, Safety factor 3.0. Span 1000mm: Uniform load 3.5 kN/m², Point load 1.0 kN, Deflection <5mm, Safety factor 3.0. Span 1200mm: Uniform load 2.5 kN/m², Point load 0.8 kN, Deflection <6mm, Safety factor 2.8. Span 1500mm: Uniform load 1.8 kN/m², Point load 0.5 kN, Deflection <8mm, Safety factor 2.5. Note: Values are for pedestrian/light industrial use. Heavy-duty applications require 50mm grating or pultruded grating. Vinyl ester resin has similar load capacity to isophthalic.

3. Molded Grating by Thickness Comparison (at 1000mm span)

25mm (light duty): Uniform 1.5 kN/m², Point 0.5 kN, Weight 10-12 kg/m², Best for: drainage covers, light walkways. 30mm (medium): Uniform 2.5 kN/m², Point 0.8 kN, Weight 13-15 kg/m², Best for: general walkways, ramps. 38mm (standard): Uniform 3.5 kN/m², Point 1.0 kN, Weight 15-20 kg/m², Best for: industrial platforms, standard applications. 50mm (heavy duty): Uniform 5.0 kN/m², Point 1.5 kN, Weight 22-28 kg/m², Best for: heavy traffic, forklift areas, large spans. Mini mesh (19×19) has approximately 15% higher load capacity than standard 38×38 mesh due to more material per area.

4. Pultruded Grating Load Table (50mm I-bar, 38mm spacing)

Span 1000mm: Uniform 25 kN/m², Point 5.0 kN, Deflection

5. Deflection Limits & User Comfort

Deflection limits are critical for user comfort and safety. L/200 (e.g., 5mm at 1000mm span): standard for industrial floors, acceptable for most users. L/240 (4mm at 1000mm): recommended for offices, areas with sensitive equipment, or where users perceive deflection as "unstable." L/300 (3.3mm at 1000mm): premium feel, recommended for public areas, retail, or where vibration sensitivity is high. Excessive deflection (>L/150) can cause user discomfort, fatigue, and perception of instability even if structurally safe. For dynamic loads (walking, running), multiply static load by 1.5 for impact factor.

6. How to Calculate Required Grating for Your Project

Step 1: Determine support spacing (span) — measure distance between support beams. Step 2: Determine required load — pedestrian (3 kN/m²), light industrial (5 kN/m²), heavy industrial (10 kN/m²), forklift (25+ kN/m²). Step 3: Check load table — find thickness that meets or exceeds required load at your span. Step 4: Check deflection — ensure deflection is within acceptable limit (L/200 or L/240). Step 5: Consider environment — select resin based on chemicals, temperature, UV. Step 6: Consider surface — grit top for wet/oily areas, concave for standard, smooth for clean rooms. Step 7: Request engineering calculation for spans >1500mm or loads >10 kN/m². ZEALL provides free structural calculations with every quotation.
